predecessors.name: Kingdom of Aksum
predecessors.text: the Aksumite heartland, Tigray and the Eritrean highlands, conquered 'around 960' by Gudit, who 'ruled over what remained of the kingdom' for 40 years before 'the last of her dynasty was overthrown…

successors.name: Ethiopian Empire
successors.text: the whole kingdom: Lasta, Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara to Lake Tana

ledger.x: 947: a kingdom in Lasta, by the early tradition.

c. 960: Gudit destroys Aksum; the highlands pass to the line the Zagwe succeed. 1137: the Zagwe kingdom at the extent Buxton describes.
1270: Yekuno Amlak kills the last Zagwe king at Ansata.
